passages.title: Article — Wedding Planning Made Easy
passages.text:
Hindle, September 9

Albert Marsh knows firsthand that planning a wedding can be a time-consuming and energy-draining endeavor. He and his fiancée had to crisscross Tindle to find vendors that suited their budget and style requirements. It occurred to him that there had to be a better way to make the necessary wedding preparations.

Mr. Marsh acted on that idea. Barely a year into his marriage, he created Nupjewel's Paradise, a company that aims to simplify wedding planning. Located at 248 Palmchat Drive, on the site of the former Harrison grocery store, the company has partnered with 50 wedding-industry professionals. Customers appreciate being able to book the services they need in one location, says Mr. Marsh. Vendors, in turn, have easier access to a large number of clients.

Mr. Marsh says he has received requests from people interested in opening their own businesses under his brand name, which would make them distributors of his services. He is open to that possibility. Just months after opening Nupjewel's Paradise, he says, it became apparent that there was a great need for his services. He cannot be everywhere at once and would welcome some help.

passages.title: Article — Video Conferencing for Hiring
passages.text:
While in-person interviews are not going away, many human resources departments have come to rely on video conferencing for candidate screening. Using video has reduced unproductive communication between job seekers and employers, and both parties appreciate the ability to schedule interviews more easily.

Finding a video-conferencing vendor can be challenging, especially for smaller companies. Libba Renwick, Human Resources Director at Adinama Clothing Manufacturers, recommends that companies think broadly about their needs. For example, she asks whether on-site meetings currently taking place could be conducted just as effectively by video conference.

Another consideration, according to Ms. Renwick, is that businesses often use the same technology for activities such as employee training. The cost savings could be significant for international companies. She cautions that potential vendors should be asked how proposed systems will be customized without creating unreasonable costs or placing a strain on information-technology staff.

Some companies may need only basic video capabilities, while others may seek advanced functions, such as built-in analytics software that allows managers to score and rank video interviews in real time.

passages.title: Editor's Note — Transport Quarterly
passages.text: The news often talks about the use of driverless passenger cars in the near future, but self-driving trucks (SDTs) will likely be transporting deliveries on the country's roadways even sooner, perhaps within the next several years. In our autumn issue, we check in with industry experts for analysis of issues related to SDTs. Jane Tilley of Tellerton Technologies takes a look at the technology that is literally driving SDTs. Leo Radosh of the Tapton Engineering Group describes advances in global positioning system (GPS) technology and the role it will play in the acceptance of SDTs.

From: Dr. Lodon Gagnon, Bunbury Institute of Technology
To: K. Moodyama, M. Solutions
Date: January 14
Subject: Visiting BIT

Dear Ms. Moodyama,

I teach an undergraduate course called Transportation and Distribution at the Bunbury Institute of Technology (BIT), which includes a unit on cost structures for freight carriers. I would like to invite you to visit my class as a guest speaker. I saw your article in Transport Quarterly and was going to assign it as required reading for my students. It then occurred to me that your company is only a ten-minute drive from our campus. My students would be very interested in your thoughts on self-driving fleets.

The class meets Tuesday and Thursday mornings from 9:00 to 11:15, and there are 74 students enrolled. I can fit your visit into the schedule at any point between now and our exams on March 12. Although I do not have a budget to compensate you for your time or travel, I would be delighted to treat you to lunch after class.

I hope you will consider visiting us at BIT in the near future.

Yours truly,
Dr. Lodon Gagnon
Department of Transportation Engineering
